classroom_why_items.title: Everything for the lesson in one place
classroom_why_items.text: Lessons, a material library, tests — no more juggling a dozen separate apps and websites.

classroom_why_items.title: Instant answer log
classroom_why_items.text: The teacher sees who's making mistakes and where, right during the lesson — no waiting to grade notebooks.

classroom_why_items.title: 3D content library
classroom_why_items.text: Material that makes the lesson up to 100% more effective and adds interactivity.

classroom_why_items.title: AI assistant for teachers
classroom_why_items.text: A resource that helps organize and build a lesson faster.

classroom_why_items.title: Works without a stable internet connection
classroom_why_items.text: Lesson materials are downloaded in advance and open offline.

classroom_why_items.title: One app for every device
classroom_why_items.text: The teacher's laptop and tablet, any student smartphone, the classroom's interactive panel.

classroom_platform_title: What's in the Eddy Classroom platform

classroom_platform_items.title: Web version for teachers and administrators
classroom_platform_items.text: Course and lesson prep, working with the library, a test and quiz builder with different question types, viewing results and the session log.

classroom_platform_items.title: The whole group takes the test together
classroom_platform_items.text: The class answers at the same time and the teacher watches a live table: who is on which question, who got it wrong, and what they scored. One button ends the test.
classroom_platform_items.shot_alt: A shared test session: the class answer table beside the question and its options

classroom_platform_items.title: Easy student access
classroom_platform_items.text: Once joined to a course, a student can easily browse its materials, complete assignments, and take tests.

classroom_platform_items.title: Interactive panel and whiteboard
classroom_platform_items.text: Front-of-class display of presentations, video, documents, 3D models and simulations; draw and annotate directly over the material in real time.

classroom_platform_items.title: Analytics and a lesson-effectiveness dashboard
classroom_platform_items.text: A clear overview of class engagement and material mastery, with recommendations for the teacher based on session results.

classroom_platform_items.title: In-lesson game tools
classroom_platform_items.text: A wheel of names for random student selection, a timer, and a noise meter — simple tools that add dynamics to the lesson.

classroom_platform_items.title: Virtual classroom
classroom_platform_items.text: Connect students to the class remotely: browsing materials and communicating even outside the classroom.

classroom_library_model_alt: Interactive 3D model of the human eye in cross-section

classroom_library_model_parts.label: Sclera
classroom_library_model_parts.desc: The tough outer fibrous coat — the white of the eye. It holds the globe's shape, protects the structures inside and gives the eye muscles something to pull against; at the front it becomes the transparent cornea.

classroom_library_model_parts.label: Choroid
classroom_library_model_parts.desc: The middle coat, densely packed with blood vessels. It feeds the outer layers of the retina with oxygen and nutrients, and its dark pigment soaks up stray light so it cannot scatter back inside the eye.

classroom_library_model_parts.label: Retina
classroom_library_model_parts.desc: The innermost light-sensitive coat — the eye's screen. Its photoreceptors turn light into nerve impulses that travel on to the optic nerve.

classroom_library_model_parts.label: Cornea
classroom_library_model_parts.desc: The transparent domed window at the front of the eye. It contains no blood vessels at all, which is exactly why it stays clear; it bends light more strongly than the lens does, providing about two-thirds of the eye's focusing power.

classroom_library_model_parts.label: Anterior chamber (aqueous humour)
classroom_library_model_parts.desc: The space between the cornea and the iris, filled with clear aqueous humour. The fluid is continuously renewed, feeds the vessel-free cornea and lens, and creates the internal pressure that keeps the eye firm.

classroom_library_model_parts.label: Iris
classroom_library_model_parts.desc: The coloured muscular diaphragm with an opening at its centre — the pupil. By changing the pupil's diameter the iris meters how much light reaches the retina: the opening narrows in bright light and widens in the dark.

classroom_library_model_parts.label: Ciliary body
classroom_library_model_parts.desc: A muscular ring that suspends the lens on fine fibres and changes its curvature — this is how the eye focuses. It also produces the aqueous humour that fills the anterior chamber.

classroom_library_model_parts.label: Lens
classroom_library_model_parts.desc: The transparent biconvex body behind the pupil. Unlike the cornea it can change shape: the ciliary body makes it rounder for near objects and flatter for distant ones.

classroom_library_model_parts.label: Vitreous body
classroom_library_model_parts.desc: The clear gel filling almost the whole volume of the eye behind the lens. It lets light through to the retina and at the same time presses the retina against the choroid from inside, holding the globe's shape.

classroom_library_model_parts.label: Optic nerve
classroom_library_model_parts.desc: A bundle of about a million nerve fibres leaving the back wall of the eye and carrying the image to the brain. There is not a single photoreceptor where it exits — this is the blind spot, and we never notice it.
